items.coverage: 1901 coverage expanded by about 2.5 million persons. Changes include Shan States, Chin Hills and Karenni in Burma, Manipur, additional frontier enumeration and new Baluchistan returns. Subtracting Aden cannot correct these changes.
items.spatial_check: In data/world_map/historical/cshapes_1900_snapshot.json Yangon, Mandalay, Kolkata, Hyderabad, Quetta and Gilgit lie in gw_750. The Aden town point (45.03 E, 12.80 N) is outside the snapshot polygons. These interior points do not certify full boundary equivalence.

items.calculation: 31 March island estimate 3,484,035 minus its reported Q1 increase 14,811. The increase comprises 9,484 natural increase and 5,327 net migration of Indian labourers.
items.coverage: The nine provinces and 21 districts in Table I use the 1891 baseline updated only by births and deaths. Their sums reproduce 3,196,686. The migration-inclusive difference has no district allocation. Maldives were outside the island return.

items.coverage: Historical figures for NSW, Victoria, Queensland, South Australia, Western Australia and Tasmania exclude part of the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander population. Complete inclusion in this ABS retrospective series begins in 1961. No all-resident opening or unobserved Indigenous count is inferred.

items.coverage: Cao includes Taiwan in Fujian and excludes Outer Mongolia. The 25 printed provincial and frontier figures sum to both national endpoints. The 1893 Xu table explicitly removes Taiwan from Fujian. The 1910 Customs column components exceed its printed total by 10 million. See qing_reconciliation.json for the dated crosswalk, arithmetic and current boundary gaps.

The official estimate combines 756,505 updated non-Māori and 39,854 Māori carried forward from the 1896 census. Published district estimates exclude Māori and therefore cannot partition the colony total.

items.locator: Appendices 2-1 and 3-1, town and markaz tables; table 4.
items.coverage: The 1897 and 1907 markaz, towns and provincial subtotals retain census-period boundaries. Urban governorates are tabulated separately. A town is included in its markaz figure. Some printed sex totals disagree with the printed total and are marked on the observation.
items.scope: The 1907 enumeration excluded 97,381 desert nomads; the nationally revised figure includes them. In 1897 the published census exceeded the later revised total by 19,880. Their geographical allocation is not established.
items.geography: The CShapes gw_651 footprint is 1,517,210 km² and contains the inhabited Kufra (23.30 E, 24.18 N), Tazerbo (21.14 E,25.79 N) and Rebiana (21.99 E,24.24 N) oases. A comparative Egyptian census geography is approximately 994,000 km². The British Foreign Office described Kufra as disputed between Egypt and Tripoli. Its report estimated up to 5,000 people in the entire group after the census dates. The Egyptian returns do not identify which of these residents were included. Wadi Halfa and Khartoum are in gw_625 (Sudan) at the opening; the southern administration was reorganized after the 1897 return. No proportional assignment of the geographic difference is made.

items.scope: gw_590 consists of two polygons only: Mauritius (representative point 57.6143 E,20.1324 S) and Rodrigues (63.3945 E,19.7086 S). Their census sums are 372,656 and 374,185. The imperial 374,879 and 378,195 return includes other dependencies and is a separate series.
